title: Co-projection composition is the mate of projection associativity
statement: Fix the finite coefficient datum of [sk-def-purity-conv], with $A=A_{E,n}$, and the bounded constructible finite-Tor pro-etale categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the constructible exceptional inverse images of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], which carry $D^b_{ctf}$ into $D^b_{ctf}$. For a separated finite-type morphism $h:S\to T$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and a tensor-invertible $N\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ [pur9-cs-def-invertible] with a chosen inverse $N'$ and evaluation $N\otimes^LN'\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$, let $$\kappa_{h,K,N}:Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N\longrightarrow Rh^!(K\otimes^LN)$$ be the morphism corresponding, under the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_T(Rh_!P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(P,Rh^!Q)$ of $Rh_!\dashv Rh^!$ used in [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], to the composite $$Rh_!(Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N)\xrightarrow{\eta^N}\bigl(Rh_!(Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N)\otimes^LN'\bigr)\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{h,Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N,N'}\otimes1}Rh_!(Rh^!K\otimes^LLh^*N\otimes^LLh^*N')\otimes^LN\cong Rh_!Rh^!K\otimes^LN\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{h,K}\otimes1}K\otimes^LN,$$ where $\eta^N$ is the triangle-normalized unit of $(-)\otimes^LN'\dashv(-)\otimes^LN$, whose counit at $Q$ is $(Q\otimes^LN)\otimes^LN'\xrightarrow{1\otimes e}Q$ for the chosen evaluation $e:N\otimes^LN'\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$; its existence with this prescribed counit follows from [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint]. Here $\operatorname{PF}$ is the specified projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection], $\varepsilon_h$ is the counit, and the remaining unlabelled isomorphisms are the evaluation, the tensor associators and unit constraints, and $Lh^*N\otimes^LLh^*N'\cong Lh^*(N\otimes^LN')\cong A_S$ through the tensor-pullback comparison $\mu_h$ of [def-exchange-projection]. (It does not depend on the choice of $(N',\text{evaluation})$; it is the conjugate of $\operatorname{PF}_{h,(-),N'}$ under $Rh_!\dashv Rh^!$ and $(-)\otimes^LN'\dashv(-)\otimes^LN$, and when $h$ is a closed immersion its inverse is the co-projection isomorphism of [lem-pur-coprojection].) Now let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Rg^!$ be the exceptional composition comparison of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition] (invertible by uniqueness of right adjoints [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], using the compact-support compositor $\alpha_{g,f}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]), and let $\mathrm{can}:L(gf)^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*Lg^*N$ be the pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Then for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ and tensor-invertible $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$: $$c_{g,f,K\otimes^LN}\circ\kappa_{gf,K,N}=Rf^!(\kappa_{g,K,N})\circ\kappa_{f,Rg^!K,Lg^*N}\circ(c_{g,f,K}\otimes\mathrm{can}):R(gf)^!K\otimes^LL(gf)^*N\longrightarrow Rf^!Rg^!(K\otimes^LN).$$ Equivalently, whenever $\kappa_g,\kappa_f,\kappa_{gf}$ are invertible and $\operatorname{coProj}_h:=\kappa_h^{-1}$, $(c_{g,f,K}\otimes\mathrm{can})\circ\operatorname{coProj}_{gf,K,N}=\operatorname{coProj}_{f,Rg^!K,Lg^*N}\circ Rf^!(\operatorname{coProj}_{g,K,N})\circ c_{g,f,K\otimes^LN}$.

source.place: Step 4(ii), etale-local comparison paragraph: the composition mate of the projection transformation

proof.text: Write $F_h=Rh_!$, $H_h=Rh^!$, $p_h=Lh^*$, and suppress only canonical tensor associators and unitors. All tensor inverses below are inverse data for the invertible object in $D^b_{ctf}$. By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], pulling back an inverse or tensoring any bounded constructible object with it stays bounded constructible, and stays finite-Tor when both factors are finite-Tor. By [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility], $F_h$ carries bounded constructible objects to bounded constructible objects. The constructible exceptional adjunctions and finite-Tor preservation are those specified in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Thus every subsequent Hom bijection can be used on bounded constructible objects; no right adjoint on the arbitrary ambient pro-etale category is used. The tensor comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] carry inverse evaluations to inverse evaluations and respect composition.

source.place: Step 4(ii): domains of the co-projection and composition comparison

proof.text: For an invertible $N$ on $T$ with evaluation $e:N\otimes N'\to A_T$, put $T_M(Q)=Q\otimes M$. Tensoring with $N'$ and with $N$ gives quasi-inverse functors: the inverse identifications are obtained by the associators, $e$, and the symmetry. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] with prescribed counit $T_{N'}T_N(Q)=(Q\otimes N)\otimes N'\xrightarrow{1\otimes e}Q$. It supplies the normalized adjunction $T_{N'}\dashv T_N$. Write $u:A_T\to N'\otimes N$ for its unit at $A_T$; its unit at $Q$ is $1_Q\otimes u$, with associators. Equivalently $u$ is uniquely specified by $(e\otimes1_N)(1_N\otimes u)=1_N$ and $(1_{N'}\otimes e)(u\otimes1_{N'})=1_{N'}$. Applying the strong monoidal $p_h$ carries these two equations to the same equations on $S$ [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], so it gives the normalized adjunction $T_{p_hN'}\dashv T_{p_hN}$.

source.place: Step 4(ii): the tensor-inverse adjunction used by the co-projection mate

proof.text:
Regard $\operatorname{PF}_{h,(-),N'}:T_{N'}F_h\to F_hT_{p_hN'}$ as a square whose horizontal adjunctions are $T_{p_hN'}\dashv T_{p_hN}$ and $T_{N'}\dashv T_N$, and whose two vertical functors are $F_h$. Its square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is a natural transformation $b_h:F_hT_{p_hN}\to T_NF_h$. The unit/counit recipe gives its component at $P$ explicitly as
$$F_h(P\otimes p_hN)\xrightarrow{\eta^N}(F_h(P\otimes p_hN)\otimes N')\otimes N\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{h,P\otimes p_hN,N'}\otimes1}F_h(P\otimes p_hN\otimes p_hN')\otimes N\xrightarrow{F_h(1\otimes p_he)\otimes1}F_hP\otimes N.$$
Here the last evaluation uses the specified $\mu_h$ [def-exchange-projection], and the first arrow is the normalized unit of step 2. This establishes the actual transformation, including its direction and sign, rather than an arbitrary map between its source and target.

source.place: Step 4(ii): first mate, across the tensor-inverse adjunctions

proof.text:
Take the square mate of $b_h:F_hT_{p_hN}\to T_NF_h$ across the two copies of $F_h\dashv H_h$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] it is $T_{p_hN}H_h\to H_hT_N$, with transpose $(\varepsilon_{h,K}\otimes1_N)b_{h,H_hK}$. Substituting step 3 is exactly the displayed defining composite for $\kappa_{h,K,N}$. This also proves naturality. For clarity, the induced map on Hom sets is
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,H_hK\otimes p_hN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes p_hN',H_hK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_h(P\otimes p_hN'),K)\xrightarrow{(-)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{h,P,N'}}\operatorname{Hom}(F_hP\otimes N',K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,H_h(K\otimes N)).$$
The composite adjunction rule [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the iterated-square identity [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] show that this is precisely conjugation of $\operatorname{PF}_{h,(-),N'}$ under the two composite adjunctions.

source.place: Step 4(ii): second mate, across the exceptional adjunctions

proof.text:
The construction is independent of inverse data. If $(M',d)$ is another inverse of $N$, write $v:A_T\to M'\otimes N$ for its normalized coevaluation. The inverse-comparison isomorphism is
$$a:N'\xrightarrow{1\otimes d^{-1}}N'\otimes N\otimes M'\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\otimes1}M'.$$
The two triangle identities in step 2 give $d(1_N\otimes a)=e$ and $(a\otimes1_N)u=v$; inserting the analogous expression with $N',M'$ interchanged cancels successive unit/counit pairs and gives $a^{-1}$. This is the usual unique comparison of the inverse tensor adjunctions [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Naturality of $\operatorname{PF}$ in its coefficient input [def-exchange-projection] makes its square at $a:N'\to M'$ commute. In the expression of step 3 the inserted $a$ from the unit and the inverse $a$ from evaluation therefore cancel. Thus both choices give the same $b_h$, and hence the same $\kappa_h$ by the bijection in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

source.place: Step 4(ii): inverse-data independence of the canonical mate

proof.text:
Let $F=F_gF_f$ and $H=H_fH_g$. The composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] has counit $\varepsilon_{g,K}\,F_g(\varepsilon_{f,H_gK})$. By the definition of $c$ [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition],
$$\varepsilon_{g,K}\,F_g(\varepsilon_{f,H_gK})\,F(c_K)=\varepsilon_{gf,K}\,\alpha_{g,f,H_{gf}K}.$$
The isomorphism $\alpha_{g,f}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition] transports the adjunction for $F_{gf}$ to a right adjunction for $F$. Both $H_{gf}$ and $H$ are therefore right adjoints of this same $F$ on the stated bounded constructible categories. The counit equation just written identifies $c$ with the unique comparison [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], so it is a natural isomorphism. This uses the standing constructible adjunctions, without assuming a separate ambient six-functor datum.

source.place: Step 4(ii): the exact counit normalization and invertibility of the exceptional compositor

proof.text:
Choose a compatible compactification tower for $f,g$. Such a tower exists: finite-type schemes over $k$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (the field has only the ideals $0,k$), hence quasi-compact, and are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; [thm-nagata-compactification] compactifies $g$, and [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle] supplies the required tower for $f$. The finite-coefficient clause of [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate], with its input called $P$ and coefficient input $N'$, gives the actual equation
$$\alpha_{P\otimes p_fp_gN'}\,F_g(\operatorname{PF}_{f,P,p_gN'})\,\operatorname{PF}_{g,F_fP,N'}=\operatorname{PF}_{gf,P,N'}(\alpha_P\otimes1_{N'}).$$
Here and below $\alpha=\alpha_{g,f}$. This is the projection identity for the canonical compact-support compositor, not an inference from abstract isomorphy of its ends.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, compatible compactification tower; the displayed projection identity is the agent specialization of lem-sf-composition-projection-mate, based on Tags 0F7B–0F7D

proof.text: The tower equation of step 7 holds for the chosen compact-support functors in the statement as well. Indeed every tensor input in that equation is bounded constructible by step 1, so has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. For each of $f,g,gf$, [lem-pur-pf-refinement-compatibility] says exactly that the compactification comparison intertwines these projection transformations, also for two choices through a common refinement. The compositor $\alpha$ is independent of choices under the same comparisons by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Conjugating the equation in step 7 by those comparisons cancels the comparisons at the intermediate objects. Finally [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identify $p_{gf}N'$ with $p_fp_gN'$ and identify their evaluations and normalized tensor units. Thus the two sides now use the specified maps of the item on exactly the same objects.

source.place: Step 4(ii): transport the projection equation through the specified compactification and pullback comparisons

proof.text:
First take mates of the equation in step 7 across the tensor-inverse adjunctions of step 2. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] applies to the two squares of step 3 for $f,g$: their common tensor adjunction on $Y$ is $T_{p_gN'}\dashv T_{p_gN}$, so their pasted mate is $(b_gF_f)(F_gb_f)$. The two occurrences of $\alpha$ change the vertical functors, not the tensor adjunctions, so clause (3) is not what is used here. Directly from the unit/counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: if a square $\gamma:L_2G\to HL_1$ is followed by $\sigma L_1$ for $\sigma:H\to H'$, its mate becomes $(R_2\sigma)\gamma^\flat$, by naturality of the unit $\eta_2$; if it is preceded by $L_2\sigma'$ for $\sigma':G'\to G$, its mate becomes $\gamma^\flat(\sigma'R_1)$, by naturality of the counit $\varepsilon_1$. With $\sigma=\alpha$ (left side, $H=F_gF_f$, $H'=F_{gf}$) and $\sigma'=\alpha$ (right side, $G'=F_gF_f$, $G=F_{gf}$) this gives the factors $T_N\alpha=\alpha\otimes1_N$ and $\alpha T_{p_{gf}N}$. Hence the equation is
$$b_{gf,P}\,\alpha_{P\otimes p_{gf}N}=(\alpha_P\otimes1_N)\,b_{g,F_fP}\,F_g(b_{f,P}).$$
Its source is $F_gF_f(P\otimes p_fp_gN)$ and its target is $F_{gf}P\otimes N$. The tensor adjunction on $X$ uses $p_fp_gN'$, identified with $p_{gf}N'$ by step 8. Since the mate correspondence is a bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], the equality is retained without an invertibility assumption on any projection component.

source.place: Step 4(ii): the first pasting, along the tensor adjunctions

proof.text:
Now take mates across the exceptional adjunctions. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with $L_1=L_2=F_f$, $L_3=L_4=F_g$ and vertical functors $T_{p_fp_gN},T_{p_gN},T_N$, says that the mate of $(b_gF_f)(F_gb_f)$ is $(H_f\kappa_g)(\kappa_fH_g)$. The mate of the compositor $\alpha:F_gF_f\to F_{gf}$ is $c:H_{gf}\to H_fH_g$ by step 6. Clause (3) of the same lemma therefore sends the two whiskerings by $\alpha$ in step 9 to the two whiskerings by $c$. Substitution yields
$$c_{K\otimes N}\,\kappa_{gf,K,N}=H_f(\kappa_{g,K,N})\,\kappa_{f,H_gK,p_gN}\,(c_K\otimes\mathrm{can}).$$
The composite adjunction here has the pasted counit of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], exactly as used to define $c$, so no alternate normalization is introduced. Inserting the identifications $\mathrm{can}$ and $\mu$ of step 8 between $p_{gf}N$ and $p_fp_gN$ (with their evaluations and normalized units) gives the first asserted equality.

source.place: Step 4(ii): the second pasting, along the exceptional adjunctions

proof.text:
When $h$ is a closed immersion, [lem-pur-coprojection] defines its co-projection to be the right-adjoint comparison induced by the projection isomorphism at $N'$. Step 4 identifies $\kappa_h$ with the conjugate of that same projection transformation in the reverse direction. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], conjugation carries an inverse to the inverse conjugate, so $\kappa_h^{-1}$ is precisely this co-projection. More generally, under the last clause's explicit invertibility assumptions, multiply the equation of step 10 on the left by $\kappa_{f,H_gK,p_gN}^{-1}H_f(\kappa_{g,K,N}^{-1})$ and on the right by $\kappa_{gf,K,N}^{-1}$. Functors preserve inverses, and the adjacent inverse pairs cancel, leaving
$$(c_K\otimes\mathrm{can})\operatorname{coProj}_{gf,K,N}=\operatorname{coProj}_{f,H_gK,p_gN}\,H_f(\operatorname{coProj}_{g,K,N})\,c_{K\otimes N},$$
which is the second asserted equality.
